deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is building a dictionary between geometric morphisms and recollement (Artin gluing) of topoi. On the previous page, a geometric morphism f : X0 -> X1 is viewed as a topos fibred over Delta_1. Its total topos X = C(f) (he calls it the 'mapping-cone'; in modern terms it is the mapping cylinder) has as sheaves the triples (F0, F1, u). Here F_i is a sheaf on X_i and u : f^*F1 -> F0, equivalently F1 -> f_*F0.

This page states the dictionary in both directions.
- Giving a geometric morphism X0 -> X1 is equivalent to giving a topos X with an open subtopos X0 and its closed complement X1, such that the gluing functor phi = i1^* j0_* : Sh(X0) -> Sh(X1) satisfies more than the automatic left exactness:
  - phi commutes with arbitrary inverse limits, i.e. has a left adjoint f^*;
  - that left adjoint is itself left exact.
  Then phi = f_*.
- Consequence: the closed inclusion i : X1 -> X is 'strictly aspherical', with a marginal '?' and '(réciproque ?)', i.e. is the converse true?
- In modern terms, the restriction i^* has left adjoint r^* : F1 |-> (f^*F1, F1, id), which is left exact. So i^* = r_* for a geometric retraction r : X -> X1 with r∘i = id; X1 is a deformation-retract-like closed subtopos of the cylinder.
- Hence i^* is exact and preserves injectives. Also Γ(X,(F0,F1,u)) = Γ(X1,F1), since a global section is s1 together with s0 = u(f^*s1). So H^*(X,F) ≅ H^*(X1,F1).
- Therefore the usual long exact sequence (S) of the open/closed pair (cohomology with supports in X1, then X, then X0) can be rewritten as (S'): ... -> H^i_{X1}(X,F) -> H^i(X1,F1) -> H^i(X0,F0) -> H^{i+1}_{X1}(X,F) -> ...
  - The middle map is H^i(X1,F1) -> H^i(X0,f^*F1) -> H^i(X0,F0), induced by u.
- He then defines relative cohomology of the morphism, H^i(X1 mod X0, F) := H^i_{X1}(X,F), with f implicit. He uses the notation H^i(X1 mod X0, F1) when F0 = f^*F1 and u is tautological.

This is the topos version of the relative cohomology of a map, H^*(Y mod X) for X -> Y, computed as cohomology with supports of the mapping cylinder relative to its far end. The problem it serves: a 'Mapping-cône' formalism giving relative cohomology / cones for arbitrary morphisms of topoi, presumably feeding into the homotopy-theoretic program of the 1980s (Pursuing Stacks, Dérivateurs era).
errors: 'commute aux lim quelconques, i.e. admette un adjoint à gauche' is slightly too quick. Between Grothendieck topoi, preserving all limits gives a left adjoint only with an accessibility / solution-set hypothesis (or by appeal to special adjoint functor theorem conditions). This is a minor gap, harmless in practice.

The asserted 'strict asphericity' is correct at the level of cohomology, via the geometric retraction r with r_* = i^*. The converse he queries is left open; it is not obviously true, since the cohomological condition only constrains Γ(X1, φ(-)) and not φ itself.
Minor: the morphism is written X0 -> X1 at the top, consistent with the previous page; the next page's transcription has a typo (X1 -> X1).

ideas.what: Geometric morphisms f : X0 -> X1 correspond to open/closed decompositions (recollements) whose gluing functor is a direct image, i.e. has a left exact left adjoint; the glued topos is the mapping cylinder of f.
ideas.modern_name: Artin gluing along f_* / (closed) mapping cylinder of a geometric morphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA4 Exp. IV §9.5 (recollement, Artin–Grothendieck–Verdier); Wraith 1974 'Artin glueing'; Johnstone, Topos Theory 1977 and Elephant (gluing, scone/Freyd cover as the cylinder of X -> Set)
ideas.where_published: Recollement of topoi in SGA4 IV 9.5; the specific mapping-cylinder interpretation is unsure

ideas.what: The closed end X1 of the cylinder is a retract via a geometric morphism r with r^*F1 = (f^*F1, F1, id), so i^* = r_* is exact and preserves injectives, giving H^*(X,F) ≅ H^*(X1,i^*F).
ideas.modern_name: cohomological triviality of the inclusion of the base of a mapping cylinder

ideas.what: Relative cohomology of a morphism of topoi, H^i(X1 mod X0, (F0,F1,u)), defined as cohomology with supports in the closed end of the cylinder, with a long exact sequence H(X1,F1) -> H(X0,F0).
ideas.modern_name: relative cohomology of a map / cone of RΓ(X1,F1) -> RΓ(X0,F0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (cohomology of a pair; in topos form, Illusie / Deligne-style cone constructions)

ideas.what: Question whether strict asphericity of a closed inclusion characterizes cylinders of geometric morphisms ('réciproque ?')
ideas.modern_name: recognition of mapping cylinders among recollements

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether a closed subtopos X1 ⊂ X that is 'strictly aspherical' (X retracts onto it cohomologically) must come from a mapping cylinder, i.e. whether the gluing functor must then be a direct image. This recognition question is not addressed on the page and does not appear to be answered explicitly in the literature in this form.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest point. It bears on recognizing mapping cylinders inside recollement situations (e.g. Lurie's ∞-topos recollement), but it is likely either false in general or a quick exercise.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct dictionary between geometric morphisms and gluings along direct images (mapping cylinders), with the resulting relative cohomology sequence. All of it is essentially known (SGA4 recollement, Artin gluing, Freyd scone). The only open item is a small converse question.
transcription_corrections: Under 'Hi_X1(X,F)' the underbrace annotation reads '{f sous-entendu}', i.e. the morphism f is implicit, not just 'sous-entendu[?]'.
The word inserted above 'un sous-topos ouvert' is uncertain; 'disjoint' is unlikely. Possibly 'disons' or 'dire que'; it is a superscript insertion before 'X0'.
Last line: 'notation aussi H^i(X1 mod X0, F1) si F0 = f^*(F1), u tautolog.'; the closing brace after 'mod X0' in the image is just a bracket.
In (S), the first term is H^i_{X1}(X,F) followed directly by '→ H^i(X,F)'; the transcription is correct.
